scenes.title: How to Complete Your OKR Self-Review

cues.text: For each Key Result, or KR, you'll need to assess two things:
its completion rate and its status.
First, check how long your KR is set for.
Is it six months, one year, or two years?
Its duration determines the expected progress for the six-month review cycle.
Our review cycle is always six months.
For a newly started KR, the target is one hundred percent for a six-month KR,
fifty percent for a one-year KR,
and twenty-five percent for a two-year KR.
Next, assess what you've actually achieved.
For example, your one-year KR may have reached thirty-five percent completion,
even though the target for this cycle is fifty percent.
Your actual completion rate is thirty-five percent.
Now use the assessment table to determine your status.
Find the row that matches your KR duration, then compare your actual completion rate with the ranges.
For a one-year KR, thirty-five percent falls within the At Risk range.
For a six-month KR, eighty-five percent is On Track.
Remember, status depends on both the duration and completion rate.
Finally, open your KR in Feishu.
Select the appropriate status,
enter your actual progress percentage,
and click Submit.
Repeat this for each KR.
That's it. Check the duration, assess your progress,
determine the status, and record your results in Feishu.
